pregame.pressurePoint: Virginia Tech deep passing vs California secondary. Virginia Tech is No. 68 of 138 in pass explosiveness (1.56). California ranks No. 101 at limiting explosive passes (1.64). A real edge, not a lock. Virginia Tech has the deep ball available. Watch whether California rolls a safety over after the first one. Watch the first deep shot. If it connects, California changes shells and the run game opens.

edges.why: Virginia Tech is No. 9 of 138 against the run (28%). California ranks No. 119 in rush success rate (38%). This is not a lean. It is a mismatch, and a prominent one. Virginia Tech erases the run. California gets pushed into passing downs, and that is where this defense makes its money.

Virginia Tech is No. 1 of 138 at the line of scrimmage (1.24). California ranks No. 104 in line yards per carry (2.82). This is not a lean. It is a mismatch, and a prominent one. Virginia Tech wins first contact. Backs get met in the backfield; screens and the quick game are the counter.

Virginia Tech is No. 12 of 138 on passing downs (20%). California ranks No. 90 in passing-downs success (29%). This is not a lean. It is a mismatch, and a prominent one. Virginia Tech gets off the field on long downs. Early-down efficiency is everything for California.

Virginia Tech is No. 46 of 138 at limiting explosive passes (1.46). California ranks No. 94 in pass explosiveness (1.47). A real edge, not a lock. Virginia Tech keeps the lid on. California should expect to drive the long way.
